title: Hearing fully and agreeing fairly

captions.energy: Gathering separate remarks into whole understanding
captions.emotions: Feeling fairness in the agreement found

meaning: A shared rule of attentive response helps you bring conversation into a whole and feel the fairness of terms considering both sides.
text: “Let’s hear each other out first” can lead to fairer consent. The Hierophant in the physical position of Vishuddha provides a recognised form of respectful reply. The World in energy seeks to connect different remarks into a whole understanding without losing what matters. Justice in emotions gives a sense of honest terms. Reassurance can come from an answer emerging after both stories are heard instead of from one particularly persuasive argument. A familiar rule serves participation, giving the question’s parts room before a final promise is spoken.

For example, you discuss a cancelled trip together. At first only expenses seem relevant, but a fuller account reveals a request to mention doubts earlier too. **Whole understanding makes an agreement fairer.** You can settle the practical part separately and name a preferred way to give notice. Terms need not be identical for every occasion; both people can explain their involvement and accept what they are actually promising after this exchange.

The difficulty arises if a wish for complete fairness creates endless reconstruction of every detail. Another explanation seems essential before the outcome can be honest. Ending on what matters preserves the rule’s usefulness. A sufficiently complete answer can apply now and leave a new request room for later discussion when it actually appears.
